title: Integrating Infinispan with RocksDB and Lucene: A Complete Architecture
subtitle: Designing an embedded in-memory data grid backed by custom RocksDB disk persistence and synchronous Lucene indexing with near-real-time index flushing.
overview: Combining an in-memory data grid with embedded disk persistence and full-text search yields sub-millisecond retrieval speeds with rich query capabilities. This architectural deep-dive details our custom integration of Infinispan with a bespoke RocksDB AdvancedLoadWriteStore backend and synchronous Apache Lucene near-real-time (NRT) indexing pipeline.
problem: Standard relational databases incur high overhead for intensive key-value reads combined with fuzzy search. Conversely, pure in-memory caches risk total data loss on node failure, and external search engines like Elasticsearch introduce network hops and eventual consistency lag. We needed embedded sub-millisecond reads, reliable disk persistence on SSDs, and instant search indexing within the same JVM process.

implementation.title: 1. Custom RocksDB AdvancedLoadWriteStore Implementation
implementation.description: Implemented Infinispan's AdvancedLoadWriteStore SPI to bridge memory entries directly to an embedded RocksDB instance with batch writing and marshalled entry serialization.

implementation.title: 2. High-Performance RocksDB Store Configuration
implementation.description: Designed custom store configuration builders controlling RocksDB block sizes, snappy compression, and memory allocations directly from externalized configuration properties.

implementation.title: 3. Lucene NRT Indexing & Worker Tuning
implementation.description: Configured near-real-time (NRT) Lucene index managers with synchronous worker execution to guarantee immediate query visibility following commit operations.
implementation.code:
indexingBuilder
    .addProperty("lucene_version", "LUCENE_CURRENT")
    .addProperty("default.indexBase", DeploymentPath.getIndexDir(false) + File.separator + name)
    .addProperty("default.directory_provider", FSExtDirectoryProvider.class.getName())
    .addProperty("default.indexmanager", NRTExtIndexManager.class.getName())
    .addProperty("default.indexwriter.index_flush_interval", String.valueOf(baseConfig.getInt("index.flush.interval")))
    .addProperty("default.indexwriter.ram_buffer_size",
        String.valueOf(Math.max(1, configValue.getLong("storage.indexBufferSize") / (1024 * 1024))))
    .addProperty("default.worker.execution", "sync")
    .addProperty("default.reader.strategy", "shared");

implementation.title: 4. Memory Management & Transaction Semantics
implementation.description: Bound the cache template to binary storage types with repeatable read isolation and optimistic transactional locking.
implementation.code:
Configuration template = indexingBuilder
    .memory()
    .storageType(StorageType.BINARY)
    .evictionType(EvictionType.valueOf(configValue.getString("eviction.type")))
    .evictionStrategy(EvictionStrategy.REMOVE)
    .size(configValue.getLong("eviction.size"))
    .locking()
    .isolationLevel(IsolationLevel.REPEATABLE_READ)
    .transaction()
    .lockingMode(LockingMode.OPTIMISTIC)
    .transactionMode(TransactionMode.TRANSACTIONAL)
    .build();

cacheMgr.defineConfiguration(name, template);
Cache<K, V> cache = cacheMgr.getCache(name);

impact: Delivered microsecond-range key lookups from memory with zero data loss on node restart via RocksDB SSD backing.
Eliminated network round trips for full-text searches by hosting inverted Lucene indices locally within the same JVM heap and filesystem.
Guaranteed strict ACID transaction boundaries across data storage and indexing via synchronized write hooks.
lessons: Synchronous Lucene indexing ensures instant read-your-own-writes consistency, but requires diligent RAM buffer size tuning to prevent garbage collection pauses during high write bursts.
Carefully isolate RocksDB native memory limits (off-heap) from JVM heap allocations to avoid container OOM-kills.
